newsitem.title: USA: Investment demand for gold fell 57 pct in 96 - WGC.
newsitem.headline: Investment demand for gold fell 57 pct in 96 - WGC.

text.p: Investment demand for gold, in developed countries monitored by the World Gold Council (WGC), fell 57 percent to 88 tonnes, a six year low, due to weak markets in Japan and Europe, the WGC said Wednesday.
Fourth quarter investment demand amounted to 18.6 tonnes, down 53 percent, the WGC said in its fourth quarter 1996 world gold demand survey published Wednesday.

"Last year saw the gold price in US dollars weaken gradually during the year, but the gains in the US dollar meant that this did not translate into lower prices in most other consuming countries and investment demand suffered as a result," WGC Americas region economist Richard Scott Ram said.
"Gold is also traditionally negatively correlated with gains in world equity markets which boomed last year," he said.
Investment demand for bullion and coins in Japan in 1996 fell to 57.2 tonnes, a five year low.

"There was significant profit taking in 1996 on the high volume of purchases made in 1995 following the Kobe earthquake when the yen gold price was also at an 18 year low due to US dollar weakness," the WGC said.

Japanese banks were increasingly reluctant to lend to the Japanese jewellery industry also, following a series of bankruptcies and this led some cash-hungry jewellers to melt down their inventories to generate income.
Full year Japanese jewellery demand was 95 tonnes, 15 pct below the 1995 level.
European investment demand fell sharply also in 1996, as the local currency gold price in Germany, the main investment market in Europe, was well up on 1995 levels.
Bullion coin sales in Germany fell 41 pct to 18.6 tonnes in 1996.
In the US investment demand for bullion coins edged up to 11.9 tonnes from 10.7 tonnes in 1995.
